messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: downloading Rstan
parts:
As Ben first pointed out, the problem here is the
following material which g++ can't (and shouldn't be asked to)
interpret:

... [1] LC_CTYPE=C;LC_NUMERIC=C;LC_TIME=C;LC_COLLATE=C;LC_MONETARY=C;LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8;LC_PAPER=C;LC_NAME=C;
LC_ADDRESS=C;LC_TELEPHONE=C;LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8;LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

g++ balks when it gets to [1], which it can't interpret.
None of this material should be passed to g++. You need to
figure out where it's coming from (hint: those values don't originate
in Stan) and get rid of it.

It appears to somehow be related to locales:

http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/locale/LC_categories

but the above is not the way to set properties on the command
line. The semicolons give it away, which will be interpreted
as end-of-command marks.

So it looks like g++ may be picking up wrongly-specified environment variables
somewhere. If you can look at your global environment variables, you
might be able to see where that is. Or Jiqiang may know what's getting included
in the call to g++ after the .o files and be able to give you a hint. Or you might
be able to do a global search (grep -R if you have to from /) on your computer to find
where these values are defined.

- Bob
